chapter: Melvin Moore, Hammond and the New York trip
title: Heading back with dates arranged by Alexander and Walter Barnes
summary: Alexander gets Philadelphia and other dates, an old contact books Chicago, and Claxton leaves.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x:
when you head back, I'm going on with South.
Anyway, I told the guys I'd see
and I got to make a little contact around and
then I talked it over with Willard. He said I
think you shouldn't go back, Fields, but I know
how you feel and it would be a little weight
off me, but he said we have representatives in
that area and they can do something, but I'll
tell you what, you went over really good down
in Philly and if you know you're going to go
back, he called a man--I don't remember him now,
but he said I think he can throw you a couple
of dates in Philly.
He said, have you got any con-
nection anywhere else? I said I think I might
play Chicago, I haven't played there before.
He said maybe I can get you one stop between
there and Chicago. So anyway, we decided we
were going to head back, and so headed on back
and this man in Philadelphia got me a couple
of dates, Alexander got about one more and I
called Walter Barnes that had a band that later

on the whole group, all but one person, was burning in the fire in Mississippi, and I knew him and I called him, and I had been getting some very good press write ups in the paper and he set me up in Chicago and I played Chicago and I think booked a date in Wichita, Kansas. And, as I told you, Rozelle, when we headed--if I remember right, Rozelle went to Philly with us and after then he told us he'd bid us goodby.

And so Chief, who had gotten in the band, also played piano and Chief sat in on piano and I contacted Hobart Banks that wouldn't come to New York City with us and when I contacted him--he used to call me Kingfish--he said I'll be waiting on you, Fish.
